newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Eight Slovaks feared dead in Danube accident.
newsitem.headline: Eight Slovaks feared dead in Danube accident.

text.p: Eight Slovak crewmen were feared dead after their tug boat struck a weir and sank in high water on the Danube in Vienna in an accident forcing shipping on the river to a halt, Austrian police said on Wednesday.

Rescue teams searching for survivors in what was believed to be the worst shipping accident on the Danube in 10 years found only one severely injured man after the Slovak-registered boat hit the weir near a hydroelectric power station late on Tuesday.
The search for the missing men continued but police said they held out little hope of finding any survivors.
"We just haven't found anything and there's very little left that we can do now," a police spokeswoman told Reuters.
The boat, which pushed a barge loaded with stone, was also missing after the strong current forced it through the weir downriver, police said.
The barge remained stuck in the weir, which was heavily damaged in the accident, and rescuers were waiting for water levels to recede so the wreck could be freed.
Until then, the Danube remained closed to all commercial traffic, police said.
The search by hundreds of firemen, supported by rescue vessels, helicopters and divers, was extended downstream to the Slovak border, about 50 km (30 miles) east of Vienna.

Water levels on the Danube, one of the most heavily-used shipping routes between western and eastern Europe, were unusually high after heavy rainfall over the past few days, but the river had been open to traffic at the time of the accident.
